content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses two aspects of Isaiah 7:14—the virgin/young-woman wording and the prophetic application—as a reason to leave the issue UNDERDETERMINED, which is the two-sense treatment K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"\"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand\": I weighed (1) treating the two aspects as two senses that both stand, so no UNDERDETERMINED, against (2) merely noting that the parties answered different subpoints without using that as a ground for UNDERDETERMINED.","why":"The judge's stated reason relies on the two aspects being separately answered to leave the matter UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2's command that a verse with two senses is not open and both senses stand."}
